extracted.intended_audience: students and scholars of philosophy and aesthetics; readers studying Kant's Critique of Judgment
extracted.subtask_description: Extracting and applying Kant's criteria for the aesthetical judgement of the sublime (mathematical and dynamic) as presented in the Critique of Judgment. Focuses on what counts as sublime, required mental operations, examples, and conditions for judgement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition — 'the sublime is that in comparison with which everything else is small'
rubrics_metrics.description: “the sublime is that in comparison with which everything else is small.” Nothing given in sensible nature can be called sublime on this basis because any sensible thing can be reduced by a different relation; the sublime lies in our Ideas and in the state of mind they produce.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Kant emphasizes that the formula shows the sublime is not a property of the object but a relation to an Idea of magnitude; telescopes/microscopes illustrate relativity of size. Must reserve exactly which Ideas for the Deduction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sublime resides in the subject’s state of mind, not in the object
rubrics_metrics.description: It is 'the state of mind produced by a certain representation with which the reflective Judgement is occupied, and not the Object, that is to be called sublime.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not ascribe sublimity to objects themselves; evaluate whether the representation invokes a mental state in which the mind's faculties (Imagination, Reason) are extended beyond sensible standards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Alternative formula — sublimity as capacity of thought surpassing sensibility
rubrics_metrics.description: ‘the sublime is that, the mere ability to think which, shows a faculty of the mind surpassing every standard of Sense.’
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Focus on whether mere thinking of something (its Idea) reveals a supersensible faculty; the emphasis is on intellectual capability (Reason/Idea), not sensible presentation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Distinction: mathematical vs aesthetical estimation of magnitude
rubrics_metrics.description: Mathematical estimation uses concepts of number (and is potentially infinite); aesthetical estimation is intuition-based (measurement by the eye) and has a subjective maximum of comprehension.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When evaluating magnitude, distinguish whether assessment is numerical/logical (Understanding) or intuitive/aesthetical (Imagination). The sublime arises specifically from the aesthetical estimation reaching its maximal comprehension.

rubrics_metrics.name: Two operations of Imagination: apprehension and comprehension
rubrics_metrics.description: Apprehension (apprehensio) can proceed indefinitely; comprehension (comprehensio aesthetica) reaches a maximum beyond which the Imagination cannot present the manifold in a single intuition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess whether the spectator can both apprehend parts and also comprehend the whole in a single intuition; failure of comprehensio aesthetica (inadequacy) is key to the aesthetic experience of the sublime. Examples: standing too near/far to the Pyramids or entering St. Peter’s.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement for pure aesthetical judgement: no teleological (purpose) mixing
rubrics_metrics.description: A pure judgement upon the sublime must not be mingled with any teleological judgement; therefore the sublime should not be exhibited in products of art where human purpose determines form/size, nor in natural things whose concepts bring a definite purpose (e.g., animals).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To judge purely aesthetical sublimity, prefer 'rude nature' that presents magnitude without charm or actual danger. Avoid evaluating man-made edifices or purposive organisms as paradigms of the pure sublime.

rubrics_metrics.name: Monstrous vs colossal — size relative to concept-purpose
rubrics_metrics.description: An object is 'monstrous' if by its size it destroys the purpose that constitutes the concept of it; 'colossal' is a presentation almost too great for any presentation and borders on the monstrous.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When assessing magnitude, check whether size undermines the very concept/purpose of the thing (monstrous) or merely strains presentation (colossal); pure sublime examples avoid monstrosity caused by purposive conflict.

rubrics_metrics.name: Aesthetical sublime arises from Imagination’s inadequacy to an Idea of totality (leading to Idea of the supersensible)
rubrics_metrics.description: When the Imagination's greatest effort is inadequate to the Idea of an absolute whole, this inadequacy excites in us the feeling of a supersensible faculty; thus the mind's awareness of ideas (of the infinite) is tied to the experience of the sublime.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate whether the representation forces the Imagination beyond sensible bounds such that Reason’s Ideas (totality/infinite) become salient; this transition from sensible failure to rational idea produces the sublime.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quality of the feeling of the sublime: respect (Reverence), mixed pain and pleasure
rubrics_metrics.description: The feeling of our incapacity to attain an Idea is 'respect.' The sublime involves pain (from inadequacy of Imagination) combined with pleasure (from accordance with rational Ideas); the experience moves the mind ('vibration') unlike the restful contemplation of the Beautiful.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In judging whether an experience is sublime, look for the paradoxical mixture: an initial painful sense of limit followed by a reflective pleasure grounded in moral/intellectual vocation. The sublime involves dynamic affect (attraction + repulsion).

rubrics_metrics.name: Mathematical sublime in intuition: large unit progression versus immeasurable whole
rubrics_metrics.description: The mathematically Sublime in nature occurs when we are given ever larger units (shortening the numerical series) until expectation of ever-greater units makes us feel boundlessness; the sublime lies in arriving at greater units rather than sheer count.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use systematic scaling (tree → mountain → earth → Milky Way → nebulae) as evidence: the feeling arises from the Imagination’s freedom and the representation of nature as nothing compared to Reason’s Ideas.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dynamic sublime: nature regarded as might that excites fear yet leaves us in security
rubrics_metrics.description: Nature considered as might (superior to resistance) is dynamically sublime when it excites fear (we think a case where resistance would be vain) but we are in safety and can take pleasure; examples include storms, volcanoes, hurricanes, tumultuous ocean, waterfalls.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To judge dynamic sublimity, the spectator must be safe (no real danger) and capable of imagining resistance and discovering in themselves a non-natural faculty of resistance (moral/mental superiority). Mere fear without safety is not sublime.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sublimity elevates self-consciousness of moral/rational destination (superiority to nature)
rubrics_metrics.description: Sublimity does not reside in nature but in our consciousness that we are superior to nature within and thus not ultimately subject to its dominion; it reveals a faculty for judging independently of nature.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess whether the experience leads to a felt superiority of the rational/moral self over natural limitations (e.g., courage, moral vocation), rather than mere thrill or terror.

rubrics_metrics.name: Modality of judgement: cultural and moral susceptibility required; less universal agreement than beauty
rubrics_metrics.description: Judgement upon the sublime requires a susceptibility for Ideas (moral feeling); therefore a higher degree of culture and development of cognitive faculties is needed, and accordance of others’ judgements is less easily promised than for beauty.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When expecting agreement about sublime judgements, account for moral/cultural formation; uneducated persons may perceive only terror. The claim to necessity is grounded on a presupposed moral feeling common to human nature rather than on immediate sensibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Aesthetic judgement classification scheme (pleasant/beautiful/sublime/good)
rubrics_metrics.description: In reference to the feeling of pleasure an object is to be classified as either pleasant, beautiful, sublime, or good (jucundum, pulchrum, sublime, honestum).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use this taxonomy to determine which category an object’s affective response belongs to: pleasant (motive of desire), beautiful (restful harmonious contemplation), sublime (movement, respect, mixed pain/pleasure), or morally good (honestum).
